findings.title: Build errors in init's errgroup closures are shared-variable races and can be silently dropped
findings.body: The errgroup closure assigns to the outer `err` (declared at line 181) and increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed` from up to `initWorkers` goroutines at once. The closure then does `return err`, which reads that shared variable, so a failing build's error can be overwritten by a concurrent successful build's nil. `init` then reports success while a namespace is missing from the index. `totalBatchesIndexed++` is also an unsynchronized write (lost updates, and the race detector flags it). This now runs inside NewResourceServer, which the code comments say must block startup on failure, so a swallowed error means a silently incomplete index. Use a closure-local error and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Watch loop dereferences nil event when the events channel is closed, causing a panic
findings.body: The loop does `v := <-events` and passes `v` to handleEvent without checking whether the channel is open. The SQL poller does `defer close(stream)` when the backend is stopped (b.done). After that, every receive yields nil, and handleEvent immediately reads `evt.Type` (line 226), which panics with a nil pointer dereference. The same pattern in server.go initWatcher (`v.Type` on a possibly nil v) panics too. The watch context is context.Background(), so this loop never exits on its own. Use `v, ok := <-events` and return when ok is false.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without the lock, racing with BuildIndex writes
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without taking cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes b.cache under cacheMu.Lock. This PR adds a new caller of TotalDocs in init (search.go line 216), which runs right after the watch goroutine has started. That goroutine can call getOrCreateIndex, then build, then BuildIndex, and write b.cache concurrently. A concurrent map iteration and write is a fatal runtime error that cannot be recovered. Take cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent duplicate builds for the same key with no dedupe
findings.body: The whole-function lock was the only serialization in BuildIndex. GetIndex returns nil for concurrent first requests, so each one runs a full ListIterator build. For file-backed indexes (size above FileThreshold), two builds now call bleve.New on the same directory at the same time (line 98). Previously the second build ran after the first and failed cleanly on the existing path. Now the two can interleave on-disk creation and fail or leave a bad store. For memory indexes, the second build replaces the first in the cache, orphaning it, and the IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics are double counted. Add a per-key guard (the TODO in search.go mentions this) or re-check the cache under the lock.

findings.title: Writes made during the initial index build are never indexed
findings.body: init lists and builds each namespace first, and only afterwards calls WatchWriteEvents. The SQL WatchWriteEvents takes its starting point from the latest resource versions at subscription time (listLatestRVs), so any write committed after a namespace was read but before the subscription is never delivered to the index. The object stays missing from search until it is modified again. This PR makes the build window longer, since the whole build for all namespaces now runs synchronously at construction. The rv returned by build (line 309 onward) is computed for exactly this purpose but discarded here. Subscribe first, build, then replay events with a resource version above each namespace's list version.

findings.title: Construction now performs DB init, full index build and watcher start synchronously, and can fail
findings.body: NewResourceServer now synchronously runs lifecycle Init (DB open and ping), the full search index build for every namespace above the threshold, and starts the watcher. Any error makes construction fail. Previously this work happened on first RPC, so construction was cheap and a failure only affected calls. The consequences: the caller (module wiring) blocks for the entire build with no timeout (only Stop cancels, and that is not reached during startup); one bad namespace or a transient DB error prevents the whole storage module from starting; and any code that constructs a server before its DB or blob dependencies are ready now fails at construction. The PR asks what this could break, but the diff shows no update to callers and no bounded context for the build. This needs an explicit decision.

findings.title: Stop no longer gates RPCs, since the Init calls that returned the stop error were removed
findings.body: Stop stores 'service is stopping' or 'service is stopped' in s.initErr. Before this PR every RPC called s.Init, which returned that stored error, so calls after Stop failed fast. This PR removes every s.Init call from the handlers, so nothing reads initErr anymore. After Stop, Create, Update, Delete, Read, List and Search keep reaching the backend. backend.Stop only cancels the poller and does not close the DB. This silently removes the shutdown guard. If it is still needed, check a stopped flag in the handlers or in a shared helper.

findings.title: Error path after the new Init call leaks started resources
findings.body: If any step after the new Init call fails, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling cancel. The lifecycle backend may already be initialized, and search init may already have started the event goroutine (search.go line 207), which loops on a context.Background() watch forever. Nothing calls Stop on the discarded server. Call s.cancel() and the lifecycle Stop on the error path.

findings.title: Span context is still discarded in WriteEvent, ReadResource and ListIterator
findings.body: The PR is described as fixing trace propagation by passing span contexts down, but this file still discards the span context in WriteEvent (`_, span := b.tracer.Start(...)` followed by `b.create(ctx, event)`). ReadResource (line 353) and ListIterator (line 388) do the same. The WriteEvent span is therefore not the parent of the create, update or delete spans, and the DB spans attach to the request instead. Only GetResourceStats was fixed here. Use `ctx, span :=` in these functions.

findings.title: Postgres skip disables the storage-server startup test without a tracked issue or mention in the description
findings.body: A postgres branch is added that skips the only test in this file covering the storage-server startup path this PR changes. The skip has a TODO and no tracking issue, and the PR description does not mention disabling it. If construction-time init broke postgres startup, that regression is now hidden rather than fixed. Either fix the test or document the skip with an issue link in the description.

findings.title: No tests cover the new construction-time failure and concurrency behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes several behaviours without adding tests: NewResourceServer now returns an error when lifecycle init or the index build fails, RPCs no longer gate on initialization, and the BuildIndex lock was removed. Nothing checks that a failing index build makes NewResourceServer return an error, which would have caught the lost-error race in search.go. Nothing exercises concurrent BuildIndex and TotalDocs under the race detector, which would catch the cache races above.
